content.text:
I've made the change and the acceptance test passes (`bin/e2e`: 1 passed). If a client has an invoice still overdue after its second reminder, you now can't send any of their drafts until the deposits held for it cover at least 30% of its grand total, even when the draft is approved. The deposits count at what they're worth after any conversion fee or card surcharge, the same as for a high-risk client.

The whole change is in one function, `depositRefusal` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/invoices/InvoiceService.java`:
- **When it applies:** the 30% rule used to apply only to high-risk clients. It now also applies to clients with an invoice overdue after its second reminder, using the existing check for that.
- **Rebilled invoices:** a draft that replaces an invoice you've rebilled is exempt from the reminder rule. If the client is also high-risk, the existing high-risk rule still applies to that draft.
- **Error message:** when sending is refused, the message gives the reason, either high payment risk or an invoice still overdue after its second reminder.

The rest of the app already worked with this, so nothing else changed: the send check, the deposit form and the existing "can this draft be sent" check all go through that function. The test only covers the main case. It doesn't cover the replacement exemption or the new error wording.
